Key visual observations:
- Corn leaf with numerous small yellowish-tan spots scattered across the blade
- **Dark purplish to black lesions concentrated along the midrib**
- Banding pattern with infected/non-infected areas alternating
- Spots are small, round to oval

This strongly suggests **Physoderma_brown_spot** — the midrib dark spots are highly diagnostic. Let me confirm with reference images.
The Physoderma_brown_spot reference (bottom-left panel) is an almost perfect match — small yellow-brown spots on blade + dark purplish-black lesions on midrib. Let me view a few more to be thorough.

All comparisons are clear. Common rust has raised cinnamon pustules, Tar spot has raised black embedded spots, Southern rust has dense orange pustules — none match the test image. The Physoderma_brown_spot reference (bottom-left panel) is nearly identical to the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Numerous small, round to oval yellow-tan spots scattered across leaf blade ✓ Physoderma
- **Dark purplish-black lesions concentrated along the midrib** ✓ Physoderma (key diagnostic feature)
- Banding pattern (infected/non-infected zones) across the leaf ✓ Physoderma
- Flat, non-eruptive spots (rules out rusts)
- No mosaic/streak pattern (rules out viruses)
